title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a permitting and compliance failure at the physical infrastructure layer of a data center, not a failure of a model or a software system. Sixty-two natural gas generators were installed and run at a Vineland site without the permits New Jersey requires for installation or operation, and the state fined the operator $1.07 million under the Air Pollution Control Act. The equipment was in service before anyone had cleared it to be there.

The failure sits in the build-out phase of a deployment that is not yet finished. The complex is under construction, scheduled for completion at the end of the year, and partly in use already, which means generators were being run while the site was still being assembled. Catching it would have taken a permit check tied to procurement and commissioning, so that no generator could be energized before its authorization existed. Instead the problem surfaced from outside: homeowner complaints about noise, violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department, and a state inspection in late July.

What is not established is intent, since the federal noise lawsuit is an allegation by homeowners rather than a finding, and the reporting does not say whether the missing permits were an oversight or a deliberate choice, nor does it establish that any AI system played a part in the siting, permitting, or operation of the generators.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators, each about the size of a tractor trailer, lacked required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said the penalty for violating the Air Pollution Control Act is the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey.

The data center is under construction and is scheduled to be finished at the end of the year. It is planned as a 2.6 million square foot complex needing 350 megawatts, enough to power a medium size city. Some of it is already in use. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit over noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders to DataOne for excessive noise.
